absent: Lower layer behaviour of poisoning, unpoisoning, kernel page mapping, guard set and clear, and safety probe primitives beyond gating conditions.
Full structure layouts for page, folio, zone, reclaim vector, alternate map, device mapping, and anonymous name beyond referenced fields.
Locking, ordering, and concurrency rules for guard, poison, alternate map, snapshot, and anonymous name helpers.
Initial values, configuration sources, and mutation paths for early boot flags, minimum order, and static toggle keys.
Error handling, retry, and recovery semantics for memory failure outcomes and page action categories.
Sequence ageing, eviction, and promotion policies for multigenerational reclaim beyond insertion choice and size accounting.
Allocation failure, lifetime, and deallocation behaviour for anonymous name handles beyond reference counting.
Architectural gate area, randomisation, node setup, sealing, and platform page behaviour outside fallback defaults.

findings.text: Page poisoning status is exposed through an early boot query and a runtime toggle query, while poisoning and unpoisoning range helpers forward to lower layer work only when the runtime query reports active.
When poisoning support is compiled out, both status queries report inactive and all poisoning range helpers become silent no operation routines that accept page range arguments and change nothing.
Allocation zeroing is required when a global default is active or when caller allocation flags request zeroed memory, while freeing zeroing depends only on its own global default.

Debug mapping helpers first perform a safety probe for unmapped state and then conditionally request kernel page table mapping changes only while a static debug toggle reports active, with a separate early boot query for availability.

Guard and debug mapping helpers have dual build shapes. Disabled shapes report inactive or zero and ignore requests, while enabled shapes expose a stored minimum order, gate guard tests and updates on a runtime toggle plus a per page marker, and conditionally change mappings.

Non preemptible page processing batch size has two build values. One derives from a thirty two megabyte span expressed in pages and the other is a single page, selecting throughput versus strict non preemption.

Gate area helpers provide a fallback virtual area lookup that yields no area and address membership tests that report outside for every input, alongside a virtual address printer that produces no output.
Address space randomisation control in this configuration is fixed to disabled.

Alternate map offset reports the sum of reserved plus free extents when a descriptor is present and zero when absent, while the companion release helper reduces the allocation count. Disabled builds always report zero and ignore releases.
Reserved virtual memory map headroom for device direct access optimisation is two pages.

Virtual memory map deduplication is permitted only without an alternate map, with a valid device mapping, with a power of two descriptor size, and when computed map pages exceed reserved headroom. One build always denies optimisation.

Memory failure handling flags form eight independent single bit options occupying successive low bit positions from zero through seven, covering count state, required action, kill requirement, soft offline, unpoison, simulated origin, no retry, and pre removal.
Memory failure outcomes form a four element ordered classification spanning ignored, failed, delayed, and recovered states.

Memory failure page categories enumerate kernel, high order kernel, compound mismatch, huge, free huge, hardware poison acquisition, unmap failure, swap cache, locked, unevictable, ordinary reclaim, truncated, buddy, direct access, unsplit transparent huge, already poisoned, direct mapping, and unknown cases.

Poison accounting helpers for pages and memory blocks are silent stubs that accept frame and count arguments and retain no state, while architecture hooks report conventional failure for memory failure handling and negative platform page membership.
Anonymous name assignment on a fallback path rejects every request with an invalid argument error, and node identifier setup plus sealing of zero page mapping are silent no operation entry points.
Unaccepted memory range probes report absence for every input and accept operations do nothing, with frame granularity membership derived by converting a frame number to a single page range.
Page identity comparison reports equality when a page content comparison finds no difference.

Page pool direct memory access index encoding reserves a low shift derived from signature geometry, a bounded bit width limited to thirty two bits, a minimum offset with an eight bit addition, plus index and magic masks that isolate encoded bits and preserve alignment.
Page pool membership test compares a masked magic field against a signature in enabled builds and always reports non membership in disabled builds.
Page snapshot groups a folio copy and a page copy together with numeric frame position, slot index, and status flags.
Snapshot status uses three low single bit indicators for faithful capture, buddy state, and idle state, with a predicate that reports faithful when the first indicator is set.

File versus anonymous reclaim classification depends on absence of swap backing, and reclaim size accounting updates both per node vector and per zone counters with optional memory control group propagation.
Reclaim size mutation requires the owning vector lock to be held by the caller, as enforced by an assertion inside the accounting helper.

Clearing reclaim flags requires that the reclaim marker is set, always drops that marker, preserves activity markers when both active and unevictable are unexpectedly set together, and otherwise clears both activity markers.

Reclaim list selection treats simultaneous active and unevictable as a programming error, prefers an unevictable sink, otherwise chooses file or anonymous inactive origin and advances to an active peer when the active marker is set.

Multigenerational reclaim mode reports switching, enablement, and fault context through static toggle shapes in enabled builds and through constant negative answers in a fully disabled build, including add, delete, and reference migration helpers that always decline.

Generation and history indices derive from sequence numbers by modular reduction, tier derives from reference counts with special handling for working set membership, and reference plus generation fields are decoded from flag storage with defined shifts and bias.

A generation counts as active when it matches either of the two youngest sequence positions. Size updates move page counts between generation, type, and zone buckets and translate addition, removal, and promotion into classic active or inactive counter adjustments, while demotion outside isolation is treated as erroneous.

Sequence choice for insertion prefers active isolation encodings, then reclaiming tail placement, then freshly allocated or dirty reclaim cases, otherwise an age penalty based on working set or referenced state bounded below by a per type minimum. Insertion refuses unevictable or disabled vectors, stamps generation state, accounts size, and queues at head or tail. Removal refuses entries without generation, preserves activity for non reclaiming active removals, accounts size negatively, and unlinks.

Vector insertion and removal first attempt the multigenerational path and fall back to classic list handling with size accounting. Head insertion avoids the unevictable list, tail insertion and removal target the selected reclaim list with signed page count updates.

Anonymous name handles use reference counting with null tolerance on acquisition and release, reuse the existing handle unless its count approaches saturation in which case a copy is allocated, duplicate by sharing into a new area, and provide a fallback allocator that always yields no object plus a no operation acquisition shape.
Inline reclaim header defines a once only inclusion guard.

Poisoning, debug mapping, and guard helpers silently do nothing when their toggles are inactive, so callers cannot infer success from completion and must not assume contents, mappings, or guard state changed.
Reclaim accounting narrows wide page deltas to a smaller signed width with a one time warning on mismatch, so oversized deltas risk miscounts.

Generation promotion and demotion assume isolation discipline. Unexpected joint active plus unevictable marking and active to inactive transitions outside isolation indicate corruption rather than supported movement.
